clue.text: Diane's pet gets a viral disease

blocks.note: Di is the short form of Diane, so Diane's becomes Di's
a pet is a fit of sulky ill humour

explanation.surface: Someone's beloved pet has caught a nasty infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like an animal, which fits the disease, but here it is the old word for a sulk or tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Distemper is a contagious viral illness of dogs and other animals, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: A herb may make daughter unwell

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
a plain synonym for sick

explanation.surface: A warning that eating a certain plant could make your daughter sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Dill is a feathery culinary plant, one example of a herb used in cooking.

clue.text: Feel unwell after group's left port

indicators.note: after tells us the ailing word follows the group word in the answer

blocks.note: a group is a set, and the apostrophe-s stands for 'is', joined on
to ail is to feel poorly

explanation.surface: Someone starts feeling seasick once their party's ship has departed.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay pieces arrive in reverse order of the clue, as 'after' says.
explanation.definitionFit: To set sail is to begin a sea voyage, which is what a ship does when it has left port.

clue.text: Record in Crete, possibly a focal point

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements the letters might take

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record
these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A music recording made on a Greek island might become a centre of attention.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicentre is figuratively the central point of activity, a synonym for focus or hub.

clue.text: Entertainer's got it taped, Iris cracked - that's about right

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so these words are smashed and reassembled

blocks.note: fodder for the rearrangement
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A performer has mastered the act while a woman called Iris has broken down, and that seems fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's about right' tells us the letter for right joins the broken-up words before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A prestidigitator is a conjuror performing sleight of hand, one kind of stage entertainer.

clue.text: What jockeys do, with nasty sort amongst them, is manage to survive

indicators.note: something nasty is twisted out of shape, so the next word is jumbled
amongst places the jumbled word in the middle of the word that follows

blocks.note: jockeys ride out on horses to exercise them
taken as written, then split open
these letters are rearranged and placed inside

explanation.surface: Jockeys with an unpleasant character among them somehow still get through.
explanation.walkthrough: To ride out is racing jargon for taking horses out on exercise; 'them' is split open just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride out the storm is an idiom for coming through a difficult period unharmed.

clue.text: Fibre's extracted from wood, Greek character recollected

indicators.note: recollected read as re-collected suggests gathering the letters back the other way

blocks.note: oak is a timber
mu is the twelfth Greek letter

explanation.surface: A fibre is drawn out of timber while some Greek person is remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person in a story but means a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Oakum is loose fibre picked from old rope and used to caulk ships' seams.

clue.text: Oscar leading wise men, mostly the first in historic NI town

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all of the word, so its final letter goes
the first in asks for only the opening letter of the next word
leading puts the NATO letter at the front of the other pieces

blocks.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the Magi were the wise men of the Nativity, here cut short
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An award-winner leads a group of sages towards an old Northern Irish town.
explanation.walkthrough: NI is Northern Ireland; 'historic' looks like part of the definition but supplies only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Omagh is the county town of Tyrone in Northern Ireland, a place in the province.

clue.text: At present everyone supports king, wise guy

indicators.note: in a down entry, what supports something sits beneath it

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
a synonym for currently
a plain synonym

explanation.surface: The whole population currently backs the monarch, says a smart alec.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the present-and-everyone words sit below the letter for king.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all is someone who acts as if they have every answer, a sarcastic sense of wise guy.

clue.text: Master's opening racist pun spoiled handwritten document

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so only the first letter of the word is taken
something spoiled is ruined and messed up, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the initial letter of the word
these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster's opening offensive joke ruined a written paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A manuscript is literally something written by hand, from Latin manu scriptus.

clue.text: Room in the Parisian grill

indicators.note: in places one word inside the letters of another

blocks.note: le is French for 'the'
an attic is a room under the roof

explanation.surface: Someone is being questioned hard in a room by a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grill' tempts as interrogation or cooking; it is the noun for a criss-cross screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a framework of crossed strips, the same thing as a grille or grating.

clue.text: Cavalryman in force

blocks.note: first meaning: a mounted soldier
second meaning: to coerce someone into doing something

explanation.walkthrough: 'In force' reads as a phrase about strength in numbers; split it, and 'force' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoon is a mounted infantryman, and to dragoon someone is to bully or coerce them, as those soldiers once did.

clue.text: Satisfy two opposing groups, as Scritti Politti do?

definitions.note: cryptic: a phrase describing what the band's name does, not a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: to gain the advantages of two contradictory positions
second, playful meaning: each word of the band's name contains the little word for a thing

explanation.surface: A 1980s pop group pleases two rival camps at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Scritti Politti were a British 1980s pop band; both words of their name contain IT, so they have IT both ways. The question mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: To have it both ways is an idiom for enjoying the benefits of two incompatible choices.

clue.text: Group's instrument of torture

blocks.note: first meaning: a British heavy metal band
second meaning: a spiked cabinet in which a victim was enclosed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Group' means a rock band here, a theme running through this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The heavy metal band took its name from the medieval spiked coffin-like device used to torment prisoners.

clue.text: Told about tardy duke

blocks.note: re means concerning
a synonym for behind time
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: Gossip about a nobleman who turned up behind schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to recount it, so related is a past-tense synonym for told.

clue.text: Poker puzzle

blocks.note: first meaning: one who prods or tickles, or a slim fire poker
second meaning: a tricky problem

explanation.walkthrough: 'Poker puzzle' suggests a card-game problem; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A tickler is something that prods, including a small fire poker, and also a dialect word for a teasing problem.

clue.text: NCO holding end of stethoscope in physical

indicators.note: end of asks for only the last letter of the next word
holding means the rank wraps around the selected letter

blocks.note: a corporal is a non-commissioned officer
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A soldier in a medical examination holds the stethoscope.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporeal means having a bodily, material form, as opposed to spiritual.

clue.text: Gathers in information about savings

indicators.note: in puts the first word inside the second
about means turned round, so the combination reads backwards

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
to gather is to understand, as does 'gets'

explanation.surface: Someone collects information on how to save money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gathers' here means understands, as in 'I gather', not collects; gen is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest egg is a sum of money saved up for the future.

clue.text: Rest day? Graduates turned up near city on the Avon

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts
Bath is a spa city on the River Avon

explanation.surface: Graduates arrived near a West Country city on their day off.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sabbath is the weekly day set aside for rest and worship.

clue.text: Car that's durable, something made for many a spin

blocks.note: hard-wearing means durable

blocks.clueFragment: something made for many a spin
blocks.note: a spinning top is a toy made to spin

explanation.surface: A tough car built for plenty of drives out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' looks like a drive in a car, but it is the toy that whirls.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardtop is a car with a rigid fixed roof rather than a fabric one.

clue.text: Capital excursion round the Italian retreats

indicators.note: something that retreats goes backwards, so the word is reversed

blocks.note: a trip is an outing
O is round in shape
il is Italian for 'the'

explanation.surface: An outing to the capital, as an Italian beats a retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital city of Libya.

clue.text: Cured haddock in a fiery broth - "more?", I ask

indicators.note: something fiery is wild and agitated, so the letters around it are stirred up

blocks.note: taken as written
fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A diner served smoked fish in a spicy soup asks for seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: Arbroath is a fishing town on the Scottish east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arbroath smokie is a haddock salted and hot-smoked, a traditional Scottish speciality.

clue.text: Poem starts to upset me in a concert hall

indicators.note: starts means only the opening letter of each following word is taken

blocks.note: an ode is a lyric poem
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A poem is beginning to distress me at a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: An odeum is a building for musical performances, from the ancient Greek odeion.

clue.text: Goddess losing credit in moment of truth

indicators.note: losing means certain letters are dropped from the word

blocks.note: a crisis is a decisive turning point
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A deity loses her reputation at the decisive moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was a major goddess of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: 'Beer' in concise dictionary in 'local' language?

indicators.note: in places the drink inside the shortened reference book

blocks.note: dict. is the short form of dictionary
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A short dictionary lists beer as a word in the pub's own lingo.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted 'local' plays on the British pub (one's local), apt with the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect is a regional form of a language spoken in a particular area.

clue.text: Difficult old emperor visiting America

indicators.note: a visitor arrives alongside the host, so the old ruler is placed next to the country

blocks.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
Nero was a Roman emperor
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A tricky old Roman ruler drops in on the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Onerous means burdensome and hard to bear, close to difficult.

clue.text: In circulation, a humorous book

indicators.note: In says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters run across the word boundaries

explanation.surface: A funny book is doing the rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Nahum is a book of the Old Testament, one of the minor prophets.

clue.text: Regroups across main road in battle

indicators.note: across means stretching over, so one word straddles the other

blocks.note: troops rally when they regroup
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway

explanation.surface: Soldiers regroup across a major road during fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramillies was a 1706 battle in which Marlborough defeated the French.
